security_implications: This chunk declares shared secret key buses (key_data[Share], sw_key_data[SwKeyShare]), entropy interface (sha3_rand_*, entropy_*), alert outputs (alert_fatal, alert_recov_operation, alert_intg_err), life cycle escalation signals (lc_escalate_en), and a mandatory zeroing of msgfifo_data[1] under EnMasking. The forced zero for share 1 assumes the secret key resides only in share 0 and will be segmented/masked later; if downstream masking fails, the full key may appear unmasked on share 0. The FSM encoding is sparse (e.g., 6'b001011) for SEU hardening but no illegal-state detection is visible; a flipped bit could move the FSM to a different but still legal state, bypassing key handling or digest protection. Entropy and error signals lack immediate containment; a stale or missing entropy, or unhandled error (sha3_err, app_err, etc.) could weaken randomness or delay fault escalation. Parameter mismatches between SwKeyShare and Share are not enforced here and could lead to key misalignment. The life cycle escalation vectors (6 copies) might face synchronization issues if not properly handled, leaving the subsystem unprotected under a critical fault.
